display.title: Episode 488: The Dike (Tisha B'Av)
display.summary_short: A Jewish girl swept away when a Dutch dike breaks forgets who she is, until the glow of Shabbos candles in a window leads her home. Plus the song of Eicha, sung for Tisha B'Av.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the Nine Days, the week of Tisha B'Av. Uncle Yossi teaches that the world stands on three things, Torah, avodah and gemilus chasadim, a 'diet' for a healthy neshamah, and stresses daily tzedakah. A first-grade yeshiva boy says the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. The story takes place in a Dutch town by the sea, where two loving sisters, Leah and little Gittel, are in school when the dike breaks. Gittel, slowed by an old injury, is left behind and is found by a harsh old woman who keeps her for three years of hard work, telling her she has no family left; with no Shabbos candles or brachos, Gittel forgets she is Jewish. Walking home alone from a fair one Friday night, she sees Shabbos candles glowing in a window, remembers her mother's Shabbos table, knocks, and finds her own family. Uncle Yossi then speaks about music as Hashem's gift, and explains that the one song we sing even on Tisha B'Av is the ancient tune of Eicha, a song of hope, which he chants. He marks Hei Av, the yahrzeit of the Arizal, and reminds listeners that the Tisha B'Av fast is this Sunday.
display.lesson: The light of Shabbos and mitzvos keeps a Jew connected to home; and even in sadness we sing with hope that Hashem will rebuild the Beis HaMikdash.

date.note: 'Today is Hei Av', the yahrzeit of the Arizal; 'this coming Sunday is Tisha B'Av' (9 Av 5751 fell on Shabbos, fast on Sunday 21 July 1991). A Tuesday.

Tisha B'Av and the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash; Eicha is chanted.
